$comment: Project-wide guard rails, checked in so they apply to every agent and every session.
The playtest tooling writes directly to a database, and live and staging share one
Firebase project and one storage bucket. dev/scripts/playtest/lib/dbGuard.js makes that
tooling structurally incapable of naming a live collection. These rules close the way
around it: the CLIs that can reach the live data without going through Node at all.
These are denials for the assistant, not for the developer. Any of them remains
available by running it yourself in a terminal, which is the point — an irreversible
operation on production data should be a deliberate human act.
